question: Summarize how to tune a random forest according to the machine learning assignment notes.
answer: To tune a random forest, define a search space for n_estimators, max_depth, min_samples_leaf, and max_features. [S1] Use stratified 5-fold cross-validation on the training data with grid search or randomized search. [S1] Select the configuration with the best mean validation score. [S1] Retrain on all training data and report the final score on the held-out test set [S1].

Assignment 4: Hyperparameter Tuning Plan
Task. Describe how you would tune a random forest.
Expected answer. Define a search space for n_estimators, max_depth, min_samples_leaf and max_features. Use stratified 5-fold cross-validation on the training data with grid search or randomized search, select the configuration with the best mean validation score, retrain on all training data, and report the final score once on the held-out test set.

S2.title: Ml Notation Abbreviations
S2.text: OOB: out-of-bag. In a random forest each tree is trained on a bootstrap sample, and the rows left out of that sample are the out-of-bag rows; about 36.8% (1/e) of the rows are out-of-bag for each tree. They provide a free validation estimate. MAE: mean absolute error. RMSE: root mean squared error. SGD: stochastic gradient descent. k-NN: k-nearest neighbors. PR AUC: area under the precision-recall curve; preferred over ROC AUC for strongly imbalanced classes. i.i.d.: independent and identically distributed. precision: in classification, TP / (TP + FP). It is not the same as measurement precision in statistics. sample: in machine learning a sample usually means one row of data (one example). In statistics a sample is a subset of a population. bias: the error from wrong assumptions of a model. The bias term (intercept) of a linear model is a different thing.
